Analysis and Decision

[8]         In exercising my discretion under section 26, I perform a gatekeeping role. Section 26(3) of the Act states: “The Chief of the Commission and Tribunals shall … review the record of the director’s decision and decide whether … the complaint should have been dismissed.” In this review of the record, I must decide whether there is a reasonable basis in the evidence for proceeding to a hearing before a Tribunal. I find that there is not, based on the limitation period in section 20(2) of the Act.

[9]         Section 20(2)(b) provides that a complaint “must … be made within one year after the alleged contravention of the Act occurs.” In Rivard v Alberta (Human Rights Commission), the Court of Queen’s Bench of Alberta noted that the Commission cannot extend this limitation period and that there is no period of discoverability.[3] The plain language of section 20(2)(b) is that a complaint must be made within one year of when the alleged discrimination occurred.

spec.key_question: What are the general rules for filing a workplace discrimination complaint, especially concerning how old the events can be or if another organization has already made a decision about them?

facts.text: The complaint must be filed within one year of the alleged discrimination occurring.
facts.why_it_matters: If the complaint is filed after the one-year period, it is generally not admissible unless there are exceptional circumstances, such as a continuing contravention or evidence outside the limitation period for context.
facts.if_changed: If the complaint is filed after the one-year period, it may be dismissed unless there is a valid exception, such as ongoing discrimination or evidence outside the limitation period.

facts.text: Events after the complaint is filed may be considered for damages but not for determining a contravention of the Act.
facts.why_it_matters: This means that while post-complaint events can affect the outcome in terms of compensation, they do not extend the time frame for determining if discrimination occurred.
facts.if_changed: If post-complaint events could be used to establish a contravention, the time frame for addressing discrimination could be extended, potentially allowing for more claims to be considered.

facts.text: A previous decision by another organization does not necessarily bar a human rights complaint.
facts.why_it_matters: This means that even if another body has addressed similar issues, a human rights tribunal can still consider the complaint, provided it is within the limitation period and not barred by res judicata.
facts.if_changed: If a previous decision by another organization always barred a human rights complaint, it would limit the ability of individuals to seek redress through multiple avenues.

facts.text: The limitation period starts when the alleged discrimination occurs, not when the complainant becomes aware of it.
facts.why_it_matters: This means that the complainant must act quickly once the discrimination occurs, as there is no extension based on discovery of the issue.
facts.if_changed: If the limitation period started when the complainant became aware of the discrimination, it could provide more time to file a complaint, especially in cases where the discrimination was not immediately recognized.

facts.text: The human rights tribunal is not bound by collective agreement provisions that may bar subsequent grievances.
facts.why_it_matters: This allows the human rights tribunal to independently assess the complaint, even if a grievance process has already been initiated or abandoned.
facts.if_changed: If the tribunal were bound by collective agreement provisions, it could limit the ability of individuals to pursue human rights claims if a grievance was not properly addressed.

facts.text: A complaint may be dismissed if it is not filed within the one-year limitation period, unless there is a continuing contravention or context outside the period.
facts.why_it_matters: This reinforces the importance of timely filing, but also allows for some flexibility in cases where the discrimination continues or requires context from outside the limitation period.
facts.if_changed: If the limitation period were more flexible, it could allow for more complaints to be considered, but might also delay resolution of cases.

facts.text: Res judicata does not always prevent a human rights complaint from proceeding if the previous decision did not address the same issues.
facts.why_it_matters: This means that even if a previous decision was made, a new complaint can still be filed if the issues are different or not fully addressed.
facts.if_changed: If res judicata always prevented a new complaint, it could limit the ability of individuals to seek redress for similar issues in the future.

facts.text: The human rights tribunal may consider evidence outside the limitation period for context, but not to establish a contravention.
facts.why_it_matters: This allows the tribunal to understand the full context of the discrimination, even if the specific events are outside the one-year period.
facts.if_changed: If evidence outside the limitation period could be used to establish a contravention, it could extend the time frame for complaints, potentially allowing more claims to be considered.

items.label: Is the complaint filed within one year of the alleged discrimination?
items.detail: The complaint must be filed within one year of the alleged discrimination, as per section 20(2)(b) of the Act [e3].

items.label: Is there a prior decision on the same issue?
items.detail: If there was a prior decision on the same issue, res judicata may apply, preventing further proceedings [e1].

items.label: Is the current complaint substantially different from the previous one?
items.detail: If the complaint is not substantially different, it may be barred by res judicata or issue estoppel [e1].

items.label: Prohibited
items.detail: The complaint is prohibited due to a prior decision on the same issue and lack of substantial difference.

items.label: Is the complaint substantially different?
items.detail: If the complaint is substantially different, it may proceed despite a prior decision [e11].

items.label: Conditional
items.detail: The complaint may proceed if it is substantially different from previous ones.

items.label: Is the complaint filed more than one year after the alleged discrimination?
items.detail: If the complaint is filed more than one year after the alleged discrimination, it is time-barred unless there is a continuing contravention or context outside the limitation period [e3, e10].

items.label: Is there a continuing contravention or context outside the limitation period?
items.detail: If there is a continuing contravention or context outside the limitation period, the complaint may proceed [e3, e10].

items.label: Conditional
items.detail: The complaint may proceed if there is a continuing contravention or context outside the limitation period.

items.label: Is there no continuing contravention or context outside the limitation period?
items.detail: If there is no continuing contravention or context outside the limitation period, the complaint is time-barred [e3, e10].

items.label: Prohibited
items.detail: The complaint is prohibited due to being time-barred.
